- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30) over recent days, reduce forecasted price increases; model tends to overreact.
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep decline, cap the peak and adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, avoid long-term trend extrapolation; favor mean reversion toward recent 7–14 day average.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in early days of 30d window, reduce initial forecast by 2–5% to account for lag.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment spikes, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast magnitude by 3–7% for next period.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, especially after 10–15 days, apply downward bias correction (e.g., subtract 1–3% per day).
- When sentiment is positive but forecast is rising sharply, check for overconfidence — reduce slope slightly to avoid “sentiment-driven overreach.”
